description: §4.12.5 + §23.4 — the CLAIMED half of the sidecar pair. A nested `<program name="ml" lang="go" …>` whose parent DOES declare `use foreign:ml { predict }` is refused at its DECLARATION with E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL, exactly as its UNCLAIMED sibling `foreign-sidecar-no-worker` is. That is the point of the pair now: CLAIMING A SIDECAR CHANGES NOTHING. REWRITTEN S356 r4 — this case previously asserted the opposite, that a claimed sidecar fires §23.4's `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` and NOT the declaration-site code. Both codes said the same thing (this execution context is specified but unbuilt; refuse rather than emit a stub) and were told apart by which SITE noticed. Three rounds tried to draw that line: an unconditional carve-out left an unclaimed sidecar with no diagnostic at all; `<program name="api" route="/api/v1" lang="go">` laundered a server endpoint past the refusal because `lang=` outranks `route=`; and the conditional carve-out that fixed the first DOUBLE-FIRED on the two ratified §23.5.4 capability cases. The operator ruling retires `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` and makes the declaration the single fire site for all four unbuilt §4.12.3 contexts. The `use foreign:` site keeps a diagnostic for its own condition — `E-FOREIGN-010`, an unresolved name — which is NOT this case: `ml` resolves.
rationale: §4.12.3 normative: "Where an execution context's codegen is not implemented in a given compiler revision, that revision SHALL emit NEITHER a reference to the context … NOR an artifact standing in for it, and SHALL fail closed with a diagnostic naming the context." One unbuilt declaration, one diagnostic, one site — whether or not anything claims it. COVERAGE NOTE (S356 r4): the harness contract is set-based (emitted ⊇ codes, emitted ∩ notCodes = ∅), so it CANNOT express "fires exactly once" — a double fire of a single code is invisible to it. Listing the RETIRED twin in notCodes catches the resurrection class, and that is the half conformance can carry; the cardinality half is pinned by COUNT in `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-sidecar-unclaimed.test.js` and `nested-program-execution-context-gate.test.js`. Artifact absence (no `new Worker(...)`, no `.worker.js`) is likewise outside the codes-only contract and covered by `nested-program-worker-artifact-emission.test.js`.
